Alright, let me think through this year's plan for my three crops.

---

**My situation this spring**

I'm 40, been farming these 20 mu since I was a teenager helping my father. Middle school education — I can read the extension pamphlets when they come around, and I understand fertilizer rates in kg, but mostly I go by what works on my own land. My wife and I do most of the work; my oldest son works in Handan most of the year at a factory, so he only comes back for wheat harvest and maize planting when we really need the hands. My younger two are still in school.

Out of my 20 mu, I keep 14 mu in the wheat-maize rotation like most people here. The other 6 mu I put into stevia three years ago after a buyer from a company near Shijiazhuang came to the village offering contracts — my cousin planted it first and made good money, so I followed. Stevia stays in the ground 3-4 years before you replant, so this is year 3 on that field. It's more work but the price per mu is better than grain, and the contract means I don't have to worry about selling it.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October)**

Right now the wheat is in jointing stage, looking decent after the spring rains. I planted Shinong 086 — it's what the agri-supply shop in the town recommends and what most of us around here use. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) down as base before planting, that's my usual. The extension guy last year said to target 15 kg pure N per mu but I go a bit heavier on the base because my soil in the south field is sandy and loses nutrients fast. I'll top-dress about 15 kg of urea per mu this week while I still have moisture — if I wait too long and it turns dry I'll have to irrigate first, which costs money from the well.

Irrigation for wheat: I did one winter watering in December, one green-up watering in mid-March, and I'll do one more at heading if the rain doesn't come. That's three times this season. I'd rather do four, but pumping costs 70-80 yuan per mu per watering and my well shares the meter with two neighbors so we argue about it. If May is dry I'll do a grain-filling watering on the best field only.

I spray herbicide once in late March — mostly for thistle and wild oats. Aphids usually show up in May, I'll watch and spray if I see them. If I get 450 kg/mu this year I'll be satisfied. Last year I got about 430 because the late-spring frost caught us.

**Maize (planting in June, right after wheat harvest)**

Same 14 mu, no-till drilled into the wheat stubble — that's how everyone does it now. The window is only 5-7 days between wheat combine and maize drill, so I hire the custom planter operator like always (40 yuan/mu for seed + planting). I'll use Zhengdan 958, same as the last three years. Some guys tried Xianyu 335 but I didn't see a big difference on our land and Zhengdan seed is cheaper at the shop.

Fertilizer: I put compound as starter through the planter, then urea top-dress at the big-trumpet stage (about 10-leaf). Around 15 kg N per mu total. I don't apply as much as the extension calendar says because summer rains usually leach a lot anyway — I learned that the year I put extra on and then we had that big August storm, the leaves still yellowed up.

Irrigation — usually 1-2 times depending on the summer. Last year I only irrigated once because the rains came on time. Pesticide: I spray for armyworm if I see damage, and corn borer is always there — the extension station hangs the pheromone traps now so I know when to go. Hoping for 500 kg/mu.

**Stevia (established, year 3 of 4)**

This is the crop that pays the bills. It's already coming up from the rootstock so I don't replant, just manage it. I'll cut it 2-3 times this season, first cut around late June, second in August, maybe a third in early October if the weather holds. The company picks up the dried leaf and grades it.

Stevia needs more water than wheat — I irrigate 5-6 times across the season, usually after each cut to get it to regrow. That's the main cost. Fertilizer-wise I use less chemical than on grain because the buyer's agronomist said too much nitrogen makes the leaves lower-quality (less steviol), so I do about 10 kg N/mu split across the cuts, plus I put down farm manure from my neighbor's sheep in the spring. Manure is cheap if you help him load it.

The labor is the hard part — cutting, spreading to dry, turning, bagging. My wife and I do it, and I pay a couple of village women about 100 yuan/day during the cut weeks. My son comes back to help if he can. If I get 180 kg dry leaf/mu at the contract price I'm doing well — stevia earnings last year were more than wheat and maize combined on the same area.

**What I'm watching this year**

Fertilizer prices went up again — urea is higher than last year at the shop. I'm not going to cut rates but I'm not going to go higher either. If diesel or pumping costs jump I'll skip one maize irrigation and hope for rain. Cash reserve matters — my son's wedding may happen next year and I need to keep something aside.
